1	# Agent usage — `internal/agentusage`
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	Two pieces: the data layer `internal/agentusage` (sections up to
7	"Verification") and the `:agent-usage` view `internal/ui/agentusageview`
8	(last section, DEVDESK-41).
9	
10	## What the package is for
11	
12	`internal/agentusage` reads the transcripts Claude Code writes under its
13	projects directory and returns, for one session, the **token counts per
14	agent** (the orchestrator and each sub-agent) and, since DEVDESK-46, each
15	agent's **tool-call count** and **time span**. It is the data layer of the
16	agent usage monitor (DEVDESK-40, spike S-01 then step S-02).
17	
18	What it does **not** do:
19	
20	- no cost, price or quota computation;
21	- no storage, no cache, nothing written to disk;
22	- no UI, no Bubble Tea import (the view lives in `internal/ui/agentusageview`);
23	- no dependency beyond the Go standard library.
24	
25	**The public API is a contract.** Every exported symbol in the table below
26	(`Tokens`, `Agent`, `State`, `Usage`, `Diagnostics`, `FileIssue`, `IssueKind`,
27	`SessionFiles`, `SubAgentFiles`, `ParseSession`, `LocateSession`, `ProjectsRoot`,
28	`ListSessions`, `Session`, `Listing`, and, since DEVDESK-44, `Cursor`, `Delta`,
29	`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `NewAggregate`, `Activity`, `ErrStaleDelta`)
30	is consumed by S-03b, S-04, S-05a, S-05b (DEVDESK-45) and S-06 (DEVDESK-46). Changing a
31	field is a change to those stories; add, do not rename.
32	
33	## Public API
34	
35	| Symbol | Role |
36	|---|---|
37	| `ProjectsRoot()` | `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, else `~/.claude/projects` |
38	| `LocateSession(parentTranscript)` | from `<dir>/<uuid>.jsonl`, finds `<dir>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` and their meta files. Returns `SessionFiles{ID, Parent, SubAgents}`. A missing session directory means no sub-agents. Returns an error if the parent is missing, is a symbolic link or is not a regular file. |
39	| `SessionFiles` | `ID`, `Parent` (path of the parent transcript), `SubAgents []SubAgentFiles` |
40	| `SubAgentFiles` | `ID`, `Transcript`, `Meta` (`""` if the meta file is absent) |
41	| `ParseSession(SessionFiles)` | returns `Usage`. Fails only if the parent transcript cannot be opened: a missing file, a symbolic link or a non-regular file is an **error**, not an ignored input. Since DEVDESK-44 it is one full delta applied to an empty `Aggregate` (see "Incremental reading"): same result as before, one code path. |
42	| `Cursor` | how far each file of one session has been read. A plain value: copying it is safe and `ReadDelta` never mutates it. Holds full paths, so `String`/`GoString` redact them (`agentusage.Cursor{files: N}`). `Rewound()` returns it with every position cleared (next read is Full): the `ctrl+r` path. |
43	| `Delta` | what `ReadDelta` found since a `Cursor`. `Full()`: read from the start of every file. `Empty()`: nothing changed. `String`/`GoString` show counts only. Applied once, by `Aggregate.Apply`, which takes ownership. |
44	| `ReadDelta(Cursor)` | lists the session again (`Lstat` only for the parent, `subagents/` and the meta files) and reads what was appended since the cursor. Returns `(Delta, error)`. Errors name base names only; on error there is nothing to apply. |
45	| `NewAggregate(parentTranscript)` | an empty `*Aggregate` for `<dir>/<uuid>.jsonl`. No I/O. |
46	| `Aggregate` | the session's usage built from successive deltas. Methods: `Cursor()` (a copy, to hand to `ReadDelta`), `Apply(Delta) error`, `Usage() Usage` (a deep copy, same shape and rules as `ParseSession`), `Activity() Activity`. **Not safe for concurrent use**: one goroutine owns it. `String`/`GoString` show counts only. |
47	| `ErrStaleDelta` | returned by `Apply`, with nothing changed, for a delta that was not read from the aggregate's current cursor. Read again from `Cursor()`. |
48	| `Activity{LastChange, Unfinished}` | what the applied reads say about the session's life. `Settled(now, quiet)` tells a poller it can stop. See "Activity and `Settled`". |
49	| `ListSessions(root)` | lists `<root>/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl`, one level deep, never recursively. Returns `Listing`. A missing root is an empty `Listing` and no error; a root that is not a directory or cannot be read is an error naming the base name only. The root itself may be a symbolic link (the user's own choice); anything below it may not. |
50	| `Session{ID, Parent, Project, ModTime}` | `Parent` is a full path, for `LocateSession`, and is never logged. `Project` is the working directory read from the transcript (`cwd`), sanitized and capped at 4096 bytes, or `""` if none. `ModTime` is the transcript's modification time. |
51	| `Listing{Sessions, Omitted}` | `Sessions` newest `ModTime` first, ties by ID ascending. `Omitted` counts what was not listed: linked or non-regular transcripts, linked or unreadable project directories, and sessions past the cap. |
52	| `Tokens{Input, Output, CacheRead, CacheWrite}` | `int64` counters; `Total()` and `Add()` saturate at `math.MaxInt64` |
53	| `Agent` | `ID` (empty for the orchestrator), `Main`, `Type`, `Models`, `Tokens`, `Messages`, `PartialMessages`, `State`, `SpawnDepth`; since DEVDESK-46 `ToolCalls`, `FirstActivity`, `LastActivity`; `PartialOutput()`, `Duration()` |
54	| `State` | `StateUnknown`, `StateFinished`, `StateUnfinished` |
55	| `Usage` | `SessionID`, `Agents` (orchestrator first, then sub-agents by ID), `Versions`, `Diagnostics`; `Total()` |
56	| `Diagnostics` | `UnreadableLines`, `OversizedLines`, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, `MetaMissing`, `MetaUnreadable`, `TruncatedFiles`, `Files []FileIssue`; `Degraded()` |
57	| `FileIssue{File, Offset, Kind}` | one skipped line or file problem. `File` is a base name. `Offset` is the byte offset of the line (for `IssueReadError`, the offset consumed; for `IssueOpenFailed`, 0). Entries are sorted by offset within each file. |
58	| `IssueKind` | `IssueUnreadable` (not JSON, truncated, or bad counters), `IssueOversized` (longer than `MaxLineBytes`), `IssueOpenFailed` (a sub-agent transcript could not be opened), `IssueReadError` (reading stopped on an I/O error) |
59	
60	`State` is read from the `finished` key of the sub-agent's meta file: `true`
61	is `StateFinished`, `false` is `StateUnfinished`. An absent, null or
62	wrongly typed key, a missing or unreadable meta file, and the orchestrator
63	are `StateUnknown`.
64	
65	`ToolCalls` is the number of distinct `tool_use` blocks in the agent's own
66	transcript (see "Tool calls and time span"). `FirstActivity` and `LastActivity`
67	are the earliest and latest line timestamps of that transcript, in UTC, zero
68	when it has none. `Duration()` is `LastActivity - FirstActivity`, or 0 unless
69	both are known; a caller that must tell "unknown" from "instant" tests
70	`FirstActivity.IsZero()`.
71	
72	## Transcript format
73	
74	```
75	projects/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl                          orchestrator
76	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl     one per sub-agent
77	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json agentType, finished, spawnDepth
78	projects/<project>/<uuid>/tool-results/                  never read
79	```
80	
81	Each transcript line is a JSON object. Only the root `type`, `timestamp`,
82	`apiBlockIndex` and `version`, and `message.{id, model, stop_reason, usage}` are
83	read; the four counters are `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`,
84	`cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`. Of
85	`message.content` (since DEVDESK-46) only the `type` and `id` of each block (plus its rank) are
86	decoded, and only `tool_use` blocks are kept (`wireBlocks`). Text, thinking, tool
87	`name`, `input` and results, and descriptions are not declared in the decoding
88	structs, so `encoding/json` skips them without keeping them. Nothing is searched
89	recursively. Symbolic links are handled by position:
90	
91	- a **parent transcript** that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is an
92	  **error** (`LocateSession` and `ParseSession`);
93	- a sub-agent transcript that is a link or not a regular file is not listed by
94	  `LocateSession`; if one is passed to `ParseSession` anyway, it stays in
95	  `Agents` with an `IssueOpenFailed` entry;
96	- a meta file that is a link or not a regular file counts as missing
97	  (`MetaMissing`);
98	- a session directory or `subagents/` directory that is a link means no
99	  sub-agents.
100	
101	## Aggregation rules
102	
103	- **Last line wins per `message.id`**, over the whole session. Streaming writes
104	  the same message several times; only the final state counts.
105	- **A message seen in several files is attributed to the last file read**
106	  (orchestrator first, then sub-agents sorted by ID). Each such overwrite counts
107	  in `Diagnostics.CrossFileDuplicates`.
108	- **A line without `message.id` counts once**, keyed by file and offset, and
109	  increments `NoMessageID`.
110	- **`<synthetic>` is excluded**: locally generated turns are never billed.
111	- **A line with neither id, model nor usage is ignored** (user and tool-result
112	  lines).
113	- **Partial output**: a message whose last line has a null or absent
114	  `stop_reason` is counted in `Agent.PartialMessages`, and `PartialOutput()` is
115	  true. Its output count is a floor. This is computed for every agent; the UI
116	  decides how to show it.
117	- **Saturation**: sums stop at `math.MaxInt64` instead of wrapping.
118	- **Tool calls and time span are folded on their own keys, not by the last line
119	  of a message** (DEVDESK-46, below).
120	- An incomplete last line (no newline) is not counted and its file is listed in
121	  `Diagnostics.TruncatedFiles`. If it already exceeds the line cap it is dropped
122	  silently.
123	
124	### Tool calls and time span (DEVDESK-46)
125	
126	Claude Code 2.1.302 writes **one content block per `assistant` line**: a message
127	with a thinking block and two tool calls is three lines sharing one `message.id`.
128	"Last line wins" would keep one block and lose the others, so tool calls have
129	their own table.
130	
131	- **Only root `type == "assistant"` lines count**, and `<synthetic>` ones never
132	  do. `api-request-blob` lines replay earlier `tool_use` blocks in their
133	  `message.content` and would double count; a line with no root `type` counts
134	  none. A `queued_command.usage.toolUses` (completion notification) is never
135	  read: the count comes from the transcript.
136	- **Key: `(message.id, tool_use.id)`.** The same pair on several lines (streaming
137	  repeats) is one call; the same tool id in two messages is two calls. The
138	  greatest position wins, as for tokens, so a call seen in two files goes to
139	  the later one.
140	- **Fallbacks, with their limits.** A block with no `tool_use.id` is keyed by
141	  `(message.id, apiBlockIndex, rank in content)`. With neither an id nor an
142	  `apiBlockIndex`, two calls of one message split over two lines both fall on
143	  rank 0 and count once: an undercount, accepted (2.1.302 always writes an id).
144	  A line with no `message.id` counts its blocks once per line (a tool id repeated
145	  inside the line counts once); each byte range is folded once, so a counter is
146	  exact there.
147	- **Ids are bounded.** A message or tool id longer than `maxLabelLen` (128 bytes)
148	  is replaced in the key by its SHA-256, so keys have a fixed size and two long
149	  ids collide only with SHA-256 odds.
150	- **Timestamps.** The root `timestamp` is parsed as RFC 3339 and normalised with
151	  `.UTC()` (the oracle compares `Usage` with `reflect.DeepEqual`, so two spellings
152	  of one instant need one representation). Anything else (absent, null, not a
153	  string, not a date) is the zero time and costs only the timestamp. Every
154	  readable line of the agent's own transcript counts, whatever its kind
155	  (`<synthetic>`, tool results, attachments), so a tool-result line moves
156	  `LastActivity`. **The span is min to max, not first line to last**: timestamps
157	  are not monotonic within a file (hundreds of backward steps in one real
158	  transcript). It is wall clock: pauses and a resumed session are included.
159	
160	## Tolerance
161	
162	The format is not a documented API, so the parser degrades rather than fails.
163	
164	- Unknown fields are ignored.
165	- A message with an id or model but **no `usage`** (absent, or renamed by a
166	  newer client) is counted in `Diagnostics.NoUsage` and adds nothing. A
167	  sub-agent with no usable meta `finished` is `StateUnknown`.
168	- Metadata of an unexpected type (`model`, `version`, `agentType`,
169	  `spawnDepth`) costs that field only, not the line.
170	- A counter that is negative, fractional or not a number makes the line
171	  unreadable (`UnreadableLines`). An absent or null counter is 0.
172	- A `message.content` that is not an array, or an element that is not an object,
173	  yields no tool call and never an error: it costs the tool count of that line,
174	  not its usage. A timestamp that is not a date costs that timestamp only.
175	- A sub-agent that cannot be opened stays in `Agents` with no tokens and an
176	  `IssueOpenFailed` entry. A read error mid-file keeps what was read and adds
177	  `IssueReadError` at the offset consumed.
178	- A missing meta file counts in `MetaMissing`; an unreadable one in
179	  `MetaUnreadable`.
180	
181	## Incremental reading (DEVDESK-44)
182	
183	`ParseSession` reads a whole session once. A view that keeps a session open
184	needs to follow it as it grows without reading a multi-MB transcript again on
185	every update. `incremental.go` (reading, `Aggregate`, `Activity`) and `table.go`
186	(the merge) do that. There is no tick, no `gen` and no UI here: wiring them is
187	S-05b (DEVDESK-45).
188	
189	```go
190	agg := agentusage.NewAggregate(parent)       // no I/O
191	d, err := agentusage.ReadDelta(agg.Cursor()) // in a tea.Cmd (Rule 110)
192	err = agg.Apply(d)                           // in Update(); ErrStaleDelta if d is not from agg.Cursor()
193	u := agg.Usage()                             // same shape as ParseSession
194	agg.Cursor().Rewound()                       // ctrl+r: next ReadDelta is Full
195	```
196	
197	### How a file is read
198	
199	Each file of the session has a read position (`fileCursor`): the `offset` just
200	past the last complete line folded in, the `size` seen at the last read, the
201	identity (`os.FileInfo`) of the handle opened, and a few flags below.
202	
203	- **Unchanged file: `Lstat` only.** If the `Lstat` size equals the size seen and
204	  `os.SameFile` matches the identity, the file is not opened. A session that
205	  no longer writes costs one `Lstat` per transcript, one per meta file and one
206	  `ReadDir` of `subagents/`, and no content read. A cursor holding an
207	  `IssueReadError` is never "quiet": the bytes after the failure are read again.
208	- **Append: read from `offset`.** The file is opened (through `openPlain`), the
209	  handle is `Stat`-ed, and the read resumes at `offset`.
210	- **A half-written last line is held back and read again.** `offset` stops at
211	  the end of the last complete line. The next read seeks there and reads the
212	  incomplete line from its start, now hopefully complete. No bytes are kept in
213	  the cursor, so a `Cursor` stays a small copyable value and a `\r\n` or a
214	  UTF-8 sequence split across two reads needs no stitching. The file is listed
215	  in `Diagnostics.TruncatedFiles` while the incomplete line lasts. Cost: at most
216	  `MaxLineBytes+2` bytes read again per file per update, only while a line is
217	  half written.
218	- **An oversized line still being written is skipped, not held.** If the
219	  incomplete tail already exceeds `MaxLineBytes+2`, the cursor stores where that
220	  line started (`skipFrom`) and the next read resumes at the end of what was
221	  read (the stored size), skipping up to the next `\n`. The line is counted
222	  **once** in `OversizedLines`, at its start. If the newline never comes, it is
223	  dropped silently, as `ParseSession` does.
224	- **Anything that is not an append restarts the whole session.** The delta is
225	  then `Full()` and every file is read from byte 0, by the same code as
226	  `ParseSession`. Triggers: a file read before is gone, is a link or not
227	  regular, fails to open, has another identity (`os.SameFile` from the open
228	  handle, so a rotation is seen), is smaller than the size seen, or the byte
229	  just before `offset` is not `\n` (a 1-byte `ReadAt` guard against a
230	  truncate-and-regrow). A per-file patch is not possible: a message overwritten
231	  across files cannot be un-counted. A file that appears (a new sub-agent) is
232	  not a trigger: it is read from 0 inside a normal delta. A first read, or a
233	  `Rewound` cursor, is Full too.
234	- **Read errors and open failures are states, not events.** An `IssueReadError`
235	  or `IssueOpenFailed` describes the *last* read of that file and is cleared by
236	  a later successful read, as a fresh `ParseSession` would show. Unreadable and
237	  oversized lines are events: counted once each, since each byte range is
238	  folded once.
239	
240	### Meta files
241	
242	`ReadDelta` never opens a meta file whose `Lstat` size and mtime did not change
243	(and that was already known). It lists them with `Lstat` instead of
244	`openPlain`; `LocateSession` is unchanged and still opens them. A meta file is
245	read again when it appears or when its size or mtime differs.
246	
247	### The incremental result equals `ParseSession`
248	
249	This is the oracle of the whole feature: for the same final files,
250	`Apply`-ing any sequence of deltas gives the `Usage` `ParseSession` gives
251	(the tests compare them with `reflect.DeepEqual`: fixtures fed in chunks, seeded
252	random sessions, a fuzz target). It holds because every line gets a position
253	(`pos{rank, off}`: the file rank in `ParseSession`'s reading order, then the
254	byte offset) and the rules are functions of positions, not of arrival time:
255	
256	- per message key, the line with the **greatest** position wins;
257	- `CrossFileDuplicates` is, over all keys, the number of distinct files minus one;
258	- models, versions and `Diagnostics.Files` follow the **smallest** position,
259	  which is first appearance in a sequential read.
260	
261	Tool calls and spans follow the same rule: a tool key keeps the greatest
262	position, a span is a min and a max, so both merge in any order.
263	`hasLines()` also counts them: **a part holding only a timestamped line (a tool
264	result, an attachment) is a non-empty delta** and advances `Activity.LastChange`,
265	while a line with neither a timestamp nor a message (`mode`, `last-prompt`) stays
266	empty. The tests' random sessions and the fuzz target generate tool and
267	timestamp lines, so the new fields are under the same oracle.
268	
269	The merge is associative and commutative. Sub-agents may therefore be read in
270	any order and appear between two updates.
271	
272	### Declared exceptions to the equality
273	
274	These are deliberate. A test that expects strict equality must avoid them.
275	
276	1. **The 100-issue cap per file keeps the smallest positions.** The cap on
277	   `IssueUnreadable`/`IssueOversized` entries (see "Limits and caps") used to
278	   keep the first 100 *to arrive*. It now keeps the 100 *smallest positions* of
279	   the file, which is what makes it independent of how reads were cut. Only
280	   *which* 100 changes, and only for a file with more than 100; the counters
281	   are unaffected. Accepted by the user (DEVDESK-44).
282	2. **`maxNoIDEntries` and `maxToolEntries` are applied in the `Aggregate`.** Past 100000 lines
283	   without a message id, which lines get no table entry (are "spilled": still
284	   counted in tokens, `Messages` and `NoMessageID`) depends on how reads were
285	   cut, not only on position. Totals stay exact (for tool calls, see "Limits and
286	   caps": a call evicted from the table counts once more if it repeats); this is the one place the
287	   merge is not commutative. Within a single merge the earliest positions are
288	   kept. The models a spill contributes are also kept by arrival order (up to
289	   the 64-per-agent cap). Not asserted equal by the tests.
290	3. **An unreadable meta file** (for example `chmod 000`) is `MetaUnreadable`
291	   through `ReadDelta` but `MetaMissing` through `ParseSession(LocateSession(…))`,
292	   because `LocateSession` opens the meta file to check it and treats a failure
293	   as absent. Because metas are compared by `Lstat` size and mtime, an
294	   unreadable meta stays unreadable after `chmod +r` until it is rewritten.
295	4. **An unopenable listed file is not a `ReadDelta` error.** `ReadDelta` fails
296	   when the session cannot be listed: the parent is missing, a link, not a
297	   regular file, or the directories cannot be read. If a listed file cannot be
298	   opened (for example `chmod 000`), or is removed between the `Lstat` and the
299	   open, the delta carries an `IssueOpenFailed` on that file: it is `Full()`
300	   the first time, then `Empty()` while the issue persists. The caller can look
301	   at the file's `FileIssue`, in `Usage().Diagnostics.Files`. `ParseSession`
302	   turns the same case on the parent into an error. When `ReadDelta` does
303	   return an error, the caller must not treat the session as settled:
304	   `Activity` keeps its last applied state.
305	
306	### Ownership and stale deltas
307	
308	`Aggregate` has no mutex: the goroutine of `Update()` owns it (Rule 110). A
309	`Cursor` is a deep copy holding no pointer, map or shared slice except the
310	immutable `os.FileInfo`, so `ReadDelta` can run in a `Cmd` while `Update()`
311	goes on. `Apply` takes ownership of the `Delta`; `Usage()` returns a deep copy.
312	
313	A `Cursor` carries the aggregate's identity and a sequence number bumped by every
314	`Apply`. A delta read from anything but the aggregate's current cursor makes
315	`Apply` return `ErrStaleDelta` and change nothing: two reads started from the
316	same cursor cannot both be applied. The caller's own generation counter stays
317	its first filter. **Rule for S-05b: keep a single read in flight per
318	`Aggregate`.**
319	
320	### Activity and `Settled`
321	
322	`Aggregate.Activity()` returns `Activity{LastChange, Unfinished}`.
323	
324	- `LastChange` is the newest mtime among the parent, the sub-agents and the
325	  metas, as of the last applied delta that found a change, capped at the time
326	  of that read (an mtime in the future counts as "now"). It is zero before the
327	  first `Apply`. A delta that is `Empty()` does not advance it, so a bare
328	  `touch` (mtime changes, content does not) does not count as activity.
329	- `Unfinished` counts sub-agents whose readable meta says `finished: false`
330	  (`StateUnfinished`). `StateUnknown` does **not** count: the quiet period covers
331	  them, otherwise a session from a client that writes no `finished` key would
332	  be polled forever.
333	- `LastChange` never moves back: if the newest file disappears, the previous
334	  value is kept.
335	- `Settled(now, quiet)` is true when something was applied, no transcript
336	  (parent or sub-agent) has an `IssueOpenFailed` or `IssueReadError` (the
337	  poller keeps trying while such a failure lasts), no sub-agent is unfinished, and
338	  `now - LastChange >= quiet`. `quiet` is the caller's parameter. A poller
339	  that stops on `Settled` stays stale if the session resumes after more than
340	  `quiet` of idleness, until `ctrl+r` or re-entering the session.
341	
342	### Known limits and risks
343	
344	- **Append-only is assumed, not verified.** A file rewritten **at the same
345	  size**, or rewritten so that the byte before `offset` is still `\n`, is not
346	  detected until the next Full read (`ctrl+r`). A reused inode on ext4 is only
347	  protected by the size comparison and the guard byte.
348	- **Check-then-open window (`safeopen.go`).** Between the `Lstat` in
349	  `readFile` and the `os.Open` in `openPlain`, a file swapped for a FIFO blocks
350	  the call. This already existed (see "Known risk" below); it is now exercised on
351	  every update that sees growth, not once per open. Possible direction:
352	  `O_NONBLOCK` on Unix. Until then, S-05b must keep one read in flight per
353	  `Aggregate`, so a blocked read cannot pile up.
354	- **Tool calls overshoot, never undershoot, past the cap.** See "Limits and caps".
355	- **The message-id table is not bounded.** The table holds one entry per
356	  distinct `message.id` for as long as the `Aggregate` lives. `ParseSession`
357	  had the same property for the duration of one call. Only line length and
358	  lines without id are bounded.
359	- **Very long `MessageID`s are not hashed.** An id of up to a line's length is
360	  kept as the map key. (The tool-call keys of DEVDESK-46 do hash ids past 128 bytes; the message table does not.)
361	- **Windows is not covered by CI** (Linux only). File identity is taken from
362	  the open handle's `Stat()`, not from `Lstat`, because Go fills the Windows
363	  identity lazily by path and would read the *new* file after a rotation.
364	  Check by hand before a release.

366	## Privacy
367	
368	`ParseSession` returns **numeric aggregates only**. No prompt, answer, tool
369	input, description or path is ever stored in a `Usage`.
370	
371	**Amendment (DEVDESK-46): the content array is walked, for block type and id
372	only.** `message.content` is decoded on every line, but `wireBlocks` keeps the
373	`type`, `id` and position of `tool_use` blocks and nothing else; text, thinking, tool name,
374	input and result are never declared. A tool id is held only in unexported fields (the line record, the tool table's key, a `Delta`'s partial table), verbatim up to 128 bytes and as its SHA-256 beyond — a size bound, not a redaction — and never reaches a `Usage`: `Agent` gains an `int` and
375	two `time.Time`, no string. The `v2.1.302-activity` fixture plants `SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` in a tool `input`, a `thinking` block, a `description`, a tool result, a user prompt and one `tool_use.id`; the tests check that no rendering of the `Usage` (nor of the parse error) contains it or the `toolu_` prefix. A tool `name` and a `text` block are covered by `record_test.go`, at the record level.
376	
377	**Amendment (DEVDESK-41): `cwd` is now read and displayed.** `ListSessions`
378	alone reads it, to tell sessions apart by project. It is the first non-empty
379	string `cwd` found in the first 8 MiB of a transcript (twice `MaxLineBytes`, so
380	one maximal line can be skipped); the scan stops there and nothing else of the
381	transcript is kept. The view shows the **full path**, with the home folder
382	folded to `~`. The path is sanitized and capped, and is **never logged**: the
383	view logs a failed listing, but its error carries a base name only. A `Usage`
384	still carries no path. This replaces the earlier wording that no path was ever
385	read.
386	
387	- Errors carry the base name of a file, never its full path (`baseOnly`), and
388	  fixed messages instead of `encoding/json` errors, which can quote content.
389	- Text that comes from disk goes through `sanitize`: labels (model, version,
390	  agent type, session and agent IDs, file names; `sanitizeLabel`, cut to 128
391	  bytes) and the `cwd` (cut to 4096 bytes). Replaced by `?`: invalid UTF-8
392	  bytes, every control character (C0, DEL and **C1**, so a raw or encoded
393	  0x9B CSI is caught) and every format character (Unicode category **Cf**:
394	  bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width marks). Text read from disk reaches a
395	  terminal, where an escape sequence would be interpreted and a bidi override
396	  would reorder what follows.
397	- `FileIssue.File` is a base name, never a path.
398	- `Cursor`, `Delta` and `Aggregate` hold full paths in unexported fields. They
399	  are never logged: `String`/`GoString` (and so `%v`, `%+v`, `%#v`) print counts
400	  only. Errors from `ReadDelta` name base names. A `Usage` still holds no path.
401	- The fixtures plant `SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` in the `content`, `description`,
402	  `cwd` and tool `input` fields of the transcripts and in the `description`
403	  of the `.meta.json` files. Tests check that it never appears in a `Usage` or
404	  an error.

406	## Limits and caps
407	
408	Memory and output size do not depend on what a transcript contains.
409	
410	| Bound | Value | Behavior past it |
411	|---|---|---|
412	| Line length (`MaxLineBytes`) | 4 MiB | line skipped, counted in `OversizedLines`, never held in memory |
413	| `FileIssue` entries per file | 100, for `IssueUnreadable` and `IssueOversized` only | counters keep counting, entries stop. The 100 kept are the **smallest positions** of the file, not the first to arrive (declared exception, see "Incremental reading"). `IssueOpenFailed` and `IssueReadError` occur once per file and are always kept |
414	| Lines without id in the table | 100000, for the whole session (all files together), enforced in the `Aggregate` | still counted in tokens, `Messages` and `NoMessageID`, but aggregated without a table entry. Which lines spill can depend on how reads were cut (declared exception) |
415	| Bytes read per update (`ReadDelta`) | the appended bytes, plus at most `MaxLineBytes+2` per file with a half-written line, plus 1 guard byte per file read | a Full delta costs what `ParseSession` costs |
416	| Tool-call entries (`maxToolEntries`) | 100000, for the whole session | a call new to a full table is counted (`extraTools`) without being remembered; a repeat of it would count again, so the total can **overshoot, never undershoot**. On a merge the greatest positions are evicted (`trimTools`, one pass over the excess when it is small, a full sort past 256) so the entries kept do not depend on map order |
417	| Message-id entries | **not bounded** | one entry per distinct `message.id`, held as long as the `Aggregate` lives |
418	| Models per agent / versions per session | 64 | extra ones dropped |
419	| Label length | 128 bytes | truncated |
420	| Meta file | 1 MiB | refused (`MetaUnreadable`) |
421	| Sessions listed (`ListSessions`) | 10000 | the oldest are dropped and counted in `Listing.Omitted` |
422	| `cwd` probe (`ListSessions`) | first 8 MiB of each kept transcript | `Project` is `""` |
423	| `Session.Project` length | 4096 bytes | truncated |
424	
425	The 10000 cap applies after the directories are read: there is **no bound on
426	memory or time before it**. Every entry of every project directory is read and
427	stat-ed first, so a very large projects tree costs that much before the cap
428	trims the result. Only the `cwd` probe, run on the kept sessions, is bounded.
429	
430	## Known risk: a FIFO swapped in between `Lstat` and `Open`
431	
432	`openPlain` (`safeopen.go`) calls `Lstat`, refuses links and non-regular
433	files, opens the file, then compares the handle with the `Lstat` result using
434	`os.SameFile`. That closes the check-then-open window for links. It does not
435	for a regular file replaced by a **FIFO** between `Lstat` and `Open`: `os.Open`
436	blocks until a writer appears, before `SameFile` can run. Closing it would need
437	`O_NONBLOCK`, which the `os` package does not offer portably. The window is tiny
438	and the attacker must already control the transcripts directory. Accepted and
439	documented in the code. `ListSessions` has the same exposure: it opens each
440	kept transcript through `openPlain` to read its `cwd`, so a FIFO swapped in
441	there can block the listing (and so the view's read, which runs in a `Cmd`).
442	Carried over unchanged, not closed. `ReadDelta` opens transcripts through the
443	same `openPlain`, so it has the same exposure, now repeated on every update that
444	sees growth (see "Known limits and risks" under "Incremental reading").
445	
446	## Diagnostics and `Degraded`
447	
448	`Diagnostics.Degraded()` is true if anything was skipped or guessed: unreadable
449	or oversized lines, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, meta
450	missing or unreadable, truncated files, or any `FileIssue`. A consumer should
451	show the totals as usual and flag them as approximate when it is true. A new
452	counter must be added to `Degraded()`.

494	`internal/ui/agentusageview`, opened with `:agent-usage` or `:au`. It lists the

496	and when a session ran at this level (see the privacy amendment above). `→` or

499	| Column | Content |
500	|---|---|
501	| Project | the `cwd`, **full path** with home folded to `~` (`theme.FoldHome`, done once per row in `Update`, never in a `Cell`). Cut from the left when too narrow, so the leaf stays visible. `-` (dim) when the transcript named none. |

510	  a failed read (red, "Failed to list Claude Code sessions — check logs"; the

596	#### Agent state and activity (DEVDESK-46)
597	
598	`status.go` derives the State column. The package describes what the transcripts
599	say; what counts as "idle" is a display policy that depends on the view's clock,
600	so it lives here, not in `internal/agentusage`. `agentStates` is pure: the clock
601	is a parameter (`statusClock{now, alive}`).
602	
603	- **`alive`** means the poll chain is live: `!Settled(at, quietPeriod)`. There is
604	  no other source (no process probe, no session registry): it also works for a
605	  transcript copied from elsewhere.
606	- **`quiet`** means `now - LastActivity > idleAfter` (5 min), **strictly**: at
607	  exactly 5 min an agent is still running. No timestamp, or a timestamp in the
608	  future (clock skew), is never quiet.
609	- **`now` is `usageDeltaMsg.at`**, the moment the read finished, not the wall
610	  clock at render time, so the same answer gives the same states on every frame.
611	
612	| Agent | Condition | State |
613	|---|---|---|
614	| sub-agent | meta `finished: true` | `done` |
615	| sub-agent | meta `finished: false` | `running`, or `idle` when quiet, whether or not the session is alive |
616	| sub-agent | no `finished` key, session alive | `running` / `idle` as above |
617	| sub-agent | no `finished` key, session not alive | `unknown` |
618	| orchestrator | session alive | `running`, or `idle` when quiet **and no sub-agent is `running`** |
619	| orchestrator | session not alive | `unknown` |
620	
621	The orchestrator is **never `done`**: Claude Code writes no end marker for it. A
622	foreground `Agent` call leaves it silent for as long as the sub-agent runs, so it
623	is not idle while one runs; if every running sub-agent is itself idle, it is idle
624	too. Once updates pause it reads `unknown`, so a session waiting at the prompt for
625	more than 5 min shows `unknown` and `Updates › paused`. Colours (Rule 122): `idle`
626	in the MEDIUM orange, `unknown` dim, `running` and `done` in the text colour.
627	
628	**The rows are rebuilt on every successful read, even an empty one** (`applyRead`
629	in `update.go`). An agent turns idle precisely because nothing arrives, so an
630	empty delta must still move the clock. `settled` is computed once and used for
631	both the clock and the decision to stop polling; while a `ctrl+r` full read is
632	pending the session counts as alive, so the header does not flash `paused`.
633	`withUsage` is `withRows` plus clearing the loading and error flags; population
634	is unchanged on an empty delta, so there is no `Remeasure` and the selection
635	stays on its agent. On `os.ErrNotExist`, `failRead` marks the clock not alive and
636	calls `withRows` (not `withUsage`), so the red footer stays. Opening or leaving a
637	session resets the clock.
638	
639	**Header.** `Idle › N` follows `Updates`, only when N > 0, counted over every row
640	(`agentTable.Items()`), not the filtered ones: an alert must not hide behind a
641	filter. No shortcut was added, so Rule 130's key set is unchanged.
642	
643	**Known limits.**
644	1. *Idle is a hint.* A long tool call (a 10-minute test run) writes nothing and
645	   reads idle. The help says so.
646	2. *Duration is wall clock.* A resumed session spans days between its first and
647	   last line.
648	3. *Clock skew.* The idle test compares the transcript's clock with this
649	   machine's; a sandbox with a skewed clock shows wrong flags (a future timestamp
650	   is never idle, a past one is).
651	4. *A lone orchestrator pauses when it would turn idle.* The chain stops at the
652	   same 5 min, so it reads `unknown`, not `idle` (see "Known limits, deliberate").
653	
654	#### Live updates (DEVDESK-45)
655	
656	The agents level follows a session that is still being written. It uses the
657	incremental API of DEVDESK-44 (`Cursor`, `Delta`, `Aggregate`), not
658	`ParseSession`: the model holds one `*Aggregate` per open session, and each
659	read applies a `Delta` to it.
660	
661	**The polling chain.** Opening a session starts a full read (cursor
662	`Rewound()`, spinner, "Reading session..."). Each answer schedules the next
663	step: wait `pollInterval` (2 s, `pollTickCmd`), then `startRead(false)` reads
664	from the cursor, silently (no spinner). At most one read and one tick exist per
665	`agentGen`: `reading` blocks a tick that arrives while a read is in flight, and
666	a tick or an answer of another generation is dropped. An empty delta changes
667	nothing on screen; a non-empty or full one rebuilds the rows (`withUsage`).
668	If `Aggregate.Apply` rejects a delta (not read from the current cursor), the
669	view logs it and reads again from the aggregate's own cursor.
670	
671	**When the chain stops.** After a successful read, the chain ends if
672	`Activity().Settled(at, quietPeriod)` is true: `quietPeriod` is 5 min, and a
673	session with any sub-agent not finished is never settled (see "Activity and
674	`Settled`"). It also ends on `os.ErrNotExist` (the parent transcript was
675	deleted). Any other error retries after another 2 s from the same cursor and
676	keeps the rows already shown; the footer says "Failed to read this session —
677	check logs", and only the first failure of a streak is logged. A successful
678	read clears the error.
679	
680	**`pollStopped`.** The model records the end of the chain as `pollStopped`
681	(true = stopped). The plan spoke of a `live` field; the code has the opposite
682	sense, so that the zero value of a fresh model is "polling". It makes a late
683	tick of the same generation start nothing, and every full read clears it.
684	
685	**The `Updates` header.** `Updates › live` while an aggregate is open and
686	`pollStopped` is false, `paused` otherwise. It is derived on every frame
687	(`updatesState`), not stored. Pressing `ctrl+r` on a settled session clears
688	`pollStopped` for the duration of the full read, so the header can go
689	`paused → live → paused` in a few frames when the session is still quiet.
690	
691	**`ctrl+r` is a full read.** It rewinds the cursor (`Cursor.Rewound()`), reads
692	everything again, and shows the spinner. If a read is already in flight, it is
693	never doubled (one per `Aggregate`): `fullPending` is set and the full read
694	starts when that read answers, whether it succeeded or failed.
695	
696	**Leaving and coming back** (`LeavingView`, see `app-shell.md`).
697	- `Leave()` bumps `agentGen`, which drops any tick or read in flight, and
698	  clears `reading` and `agentsLoading`. The open session and its rows stay. If
699	  a full read was in flight (a `ctrl+r`, or the open's first read), `Leave` sets
700	  `fullPending`, so the resume repeats it. It always returns `true`.
701	- `switchView` calls `Init()` on every entry; at the agents level `Init` adds
702	  `resumeCmd()`, which answers `agentsResumeMsg`. `handleResume` bumps
703	  `agentGen` again, clears `pollStopped` and starts a read from the cursor,
704	  silent: coming back reads what changed while away, and goes back to live if
705	  the session is still being written. With `fullPending`, the read is full and
706	  has its spinner.
707	
708	**The cursor stays on the same agent.** `selection.go` gives each agent a
709	stable key: `main` for the orchestrator, `sub:<ID>#n` for a sub-agent, `n`
710	counting the earlier agents with the same ID (two twins with one ID keep their
711	own keys). Keys are computed on the canonical order (`agentRows`), never on the
712	sorted or filtered one, otherwise twins would swap keys whenever they swap
713	ranks. `withUsage` records the key under the cursor before rebuilding the rows
714	and puts the cursor back on it, whatever the filter and the sort did to the
715	order; if the agent is gone, the cursor is clamped.
716	
717	**Column widths are not reshuffled every two seconds.** `withUsage` calls
718	`Remeasure()` only after a full read, or when the *population* changed. The
719	population is the list of keys plus the models of each row (`populationOf`):
720	counts change on every delta and do not count. An agent's type can arrive late
721	(its meta file is written after its transcript); the type is deliberately not
722	part of the population, so a late type stays truncated to the width measured
723	earlier until the next `ctrl+r` or change of population.
724	
725	**The sessions list is not live.** Only the open session is polled. The list
726	of sessions is read on entry and by `ctrl+r` at the sessions level.
727	
728	**Privacy.** `usageDeltaMsg` implements `String` and `GoString` so that `%v`
729	and `%+v`, `%#v` print only `gen`, the delta's own redacted form and whether
730	the read failed. A `Delta` holds file paths behind unexported fields, which
731	`fmt` cannot hand to the `Delta`'s redacting methods when the message is
732	dumped. Read errors are logged and never shown.
733	
734	**Known limits, deliberate.**
735	1. *An unreadable parent shows an empty orchestrator.* If the parent
736	   transcript exists but cannot be read (for instance `chmod 000`),
737	   `ReadDelta` returns `err == nil`: the screen shows an orchestrator at 0 and
738	   the warning "Totals are approximate…", where the earlier `ParseSession`
739	   path showed the red "Failed to read this session" footer. Accepted by the
740	   product owner; it is documented here rather than worked around.
741	2. *A session that resumes after `Settled` stays `paused`.* Once the chain has
742	   stopped on a quiet session, nothing polls the file any more. The header
743	   keeps saying `paused` until `ctrl+r` or until the user leaves the view and
744	   comes back (the resume reads the cursor and restarts the chain).
745	3. *A failed `ctrl+r` full read is not replayed.* If the full read started by
746	   `ctrl+r` fails for a cause other than `ErrNotExist`, the retry starts from
747	   the aggregate's cursor and does not rewind it: the `ctrl+r` is lost, and
748	   only the red footer says that something failed. Press `ctrl+r` again.
749	4. *Some exits do not call `Leave`.* The paths that leave the view by another
750	   means than `switchView` (the viewer, netdiag, the path picker) are not
751	   reachable from `:agent-usage` today. If one is added, it has to stop the
752	   chain the way `Leave` does, or a poll would continue under another view.
753	
754	**Privacy.** The view displays the project directory, the date, the session ID,
755	agent types, models, token counts, states, tool-call counts and durations. It
756	never displays or logs the paths of files a session touched, nor any content
757	(prompt, reply, tool name, input or output):
758	`Usage` holds numbers and labels only, as stated in "Privacy" above.
759	
760	Known limits: the FIFO risk and the lack of a memory or time bound before the
761	10000-session cap (see "Limits and caps") both apply to this view's read. Claude
762	Code deletes old transcripts itself (30 days by default), so older sessions
763	disappear from the list.
764

1	# Configuration — the schema and the view
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## Configuration System
7	
8	Config loaded from `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` with schema defined in `internal/config/config.go`:
9	- `App` - Global settings (theme, default view, workspaces dir, `show_hidden_files`, `secret_backend`, `gauge_glyph`)
10	- `Status` - Monitoring settings (refresh interval, components)
11	- `Forge` - the platform this context targets: `type`, URL and clone settings
12	- `Registry` - OCI registry configuration (see Registry model below)
13	- `Scan` - Security scanning: `categories` (what a scan looks for, and which
14	  tools run each one) and `tools` (one block per scanner — see `scanning.md`)
15	- `Network` - what the netdiag view runs on: the tool image, and the dials
16	  `internal/netcheck` used to hardcode; and `proxy_port` (8080), the one port
17	  every named forward route is served on (§3.74, see `network.md`) — at or above
18	  1024, and replaced by the default with a log line when it is not
19	- `MCP` - the read-only MCP server (§3.38): `enabled`, off by default, and
20	  `expose`, an allow-list of tool names
21	
22	**`forge:` was `gitlab:`, and the rename is migrated rather than announced.**
23	A context targets one platform (§3.6), so the section is named after the role
24	rather than after the one implementation there was, and it gains a `type:` —
25	`gitlab` or `github`, **declared, never sniffed**, on the registry `provider`
26	precedent. An absent `type` means `gitlab`, which is what every file written
27	before the key existed meant.
28	
29	`migrateGitLabSection` runs **first** in `applyDefaults`, and that ordering is
30	the whole of it. Every default below writes into `cfg.Forge`, so a migration
31	placed after them finds a block that is no longer empty, takes the
32	field-by-field path, and silently drops the user's own `parallel_jobs: 7` — that
33	is not a hazard imagined for the comment, it is what the first draft did and
34	what `TestAConfigCarryingRetiredKeysStillLoads` caught. The other half of the
35	reason is `docker:` → `network:`'s: `yaml.Unmarshal` is not strict here, so an
36	un-migrated block is dropped in silence, and the silence would point a context
37	at no host at all.
38	
39	**A whole-block copy when `forge:` is absent, field by field when both are
40	present.** The distinction exists for one field: `IncludeArchived` is a bool, so
41	"unset" and "deliberately false" are the same value and no per-field guard can
42	tell them apart — it can only be carried over when the new block says nothing at
43	all. When both are present the new one wins field by field: its values were
44	written later, and overwriting them with the old ones would undo the edit that
45	created the situation.
46	
47	`forge.type` is stated in `internal/config` and in each backend's `Shape()`, and
48	`TestTheForgeVocabularyMatchesTheConfig` holds the two in step — config must not
49	import a backend, and a backend must not be the authority on what a config file
50	may say, so a test is the only thing that can. Same arrangement as the registry
51	`provider` names.
52	
53	The legacy secret migration is unaffected and the order is worth knowing:
54	`credentials.MigrateLegacySecrets` reads the **raw file** at router
55	construction, before anything can save, so a plaintext `gitlab.token` reaches
56	the store before the rename can rewrite the file without it.
57	
58	**`network:` was `docker:`.** The one key `docker:` held was never a Docker
59	setting, and the four other tabs of the configuration view are each named
60	after the section they write. That key — the image the OCI connectivity test
61	ran — has since been removed along with the feature itself; `NetworkConfig`
62	now holds only the netdiag dials (`CheckTimeout`, `PingCount`,
63	`CertExpiryWarnDays`, `PortsRefreshInterval`).
64	
65	**`scan:` was flat, and it is now `categories:` + `tools:` (§3.86).** Six
66	tools had grown three to five keys each, side by side with six `enable_*`
67	switches that named categories and tools interchangeably. `migrateScanSection`
68	(`scan_migrate.go`) runs right after `migrateGitLabSection`, before the
69	defaults, on the same model: field by field, only where the new value is empty,
70	the old keys held in `ScanConfig.Legacy` (inline, every tag `omitempty`) and
71	cleared so they leave the file on the next save. Two points of its own:
72	
73	- **The categories are carried whole or not at all.** A `categories:` block that
74	  is present is an answer, even all off; mixing it with the old switches would
75	  make one category's state depend on which file wrote it. The historical "all
76	  switches off means never configured" reading survives **only** inside the
77	  migration — the one place that still sees the switches. A file with no
78	  `categories:` at all gets `DefaultScanCategories()`; an empty tool list counts
79	  as absent, because a zero `Config` saves `tools: []`.
80	- **One change of meaning, on purpose.** `enable_k8s_schema` ticks kubeconform
81	  *and* helm and kustomize, which used to serve whenever installed and are now
82	  required: what is ticked is what the dashboard reports missing.
83	
84	A category's `tools` list is a slice, so a `Config` copied by value shares it:
85	`CategoryConfig.With` always builds a new one rather than editing in place.
86	
87	**`app.gauge_glyph`** picks the fill of the containers load gauges and of the
88	netdiag waterfall: `shade` (the default — `░` for fill and track alike, told
89	apart by colour) or `block` (`█` over a `░` track). `block` is an opt-in because
90	`█` is East Asian ambiguous width and overflows the gauge columns on a terminal
91	that draws it double-width. It is not derived from the locale: the locale says
92	how the process *measures*, not what the terminal *draws* (§3.96). It is applied
93	through `theme.SetGaugeGlyph` at startup, on a context switch and on every save,
94	and anything but `block` stays on the safe glyph.
95	
96	**`app.container_engine`** names the engine every container, image, network and
97	volume comes from: `auto` (the default — docker if it is on PATH, else podman),
98	`docker`, `podman`, or an explicit path to a binary. It sits in `app` beside
99	`ide_command` and `terminal_command` — the section that already holds the
100	external tools this application drives — and deliberately **not** in `network:`,
101	which carries only netcheck's dials despite its old name (§3.67).
102	
103	`auto` is written on load rather than left empty, for the same reason
104	`secret_backend` is: `engine.Resolve` reads `""` as auto either way, but the
105	configuration view cycles a closed set and a value outside it has nowhere to
106	start from. The names are stated in `internal/config` and in `internal/engine`,
107	held in step by `TestEveryConfiguredEngineHasAShape` — the same arrangement as
108	`forge.type`, one paragraph up. The field settles **on blur**, like the forge:
109	cycling auto → docker → podman would otherwise re-resolve three times.
110	`ConfigSavedMsg.EngineChanged` is what tells the router, because rebuilding the
111	views is not enough on its own — they would be rebuilt against the engine that
112	is still resolved.
113	
114	**No secret goes in this file.** `GitLabConfig` has no `Token` and
115	`RegistryConfig` has no `Password`; both live in the host secret store (see
116	Credentials Management). Do not add a secret-bearing field back — the schema is
117	what makes the guarantee checkable.
118	
119	**`~/.devdesk/trust.yaml` is not a context file** (§3.82). It holds whom to
120	trust for image signatures — a fact about the world — so it is global, read by
121	`internal/trust`, and **strict** where `config.Load` is not: `KnownFields(true)`,
122	`version: 1`, and any error rejects the whole file (a typo would otherwise
123	weaken a rule in silence). It is edited by hand; the configuration view does not
124	touch it. Whether to verify at all is per context: `scan.image_verification`,
125	`on` or `off`, a string rather than a bool so a file written before the key
126	reads as `on` (D12) — and only `off` turns it off, so a typo verifies.
127	
128	Config is injected into views at creation. Use `config.Save()` to persist changes.
129	
130	## Configuration view — `internal/ui/configuration`
131	
132	Edits every **scalar** setting a context carries, in seven tabs (`app`, the
133	forge's own name, `scan`, `tools`, `network`, `mcp`, `status`). The second is titled after the
134	platform the context targets — `gitlab` or `github` — rather than after the
135	section key: `forge:` is what the file says, and no user calls it that. Lists stay where they are consulted: monitors keep
136	their CRUD in `status`, registries keep `RegistryForm` in `oci-resources`.
137	Duplicating them here would be the opposite of the point.
138	
139	Tabs are not decoration. Rule 135 reserves `Tab` for tabs and `↑↓` for fields,
140	so a tabbed form is the only layout where both keys have exactly one job.
141	
142	Settings are declared as a table of `field` values in `fields.go`, each holding
143	**one pointer accessor** into the config (`func(*config.Config) *string`) rather
144	than a get/set pair. Twenty-nine settings with two closures each is where the
145	copy-paste defects of §2 came from; one reference means the read and the write
146	cannot disagree about which setting they mean.
147	`TestEveryFieldCarriesTheAccessorItsKindNeeds` and
148	`TestNoTwoFieldsAddressTheSameSetting` are what keep the table honest.
149	
150	Fields inside a tab are grouped under a heading with a Nerd Font icon
151	(`SubTitleStyle`, the same treatment the security form used). `group()` stamps the
152	heading onto a contiguous run rather than each field carrying its own, so a run
153	cannot be split by a typo and render its heading twice —
154	`TestEachTabRendersItsGroupHeadingsOnceInOrder` pins that.
155	
156	**`scan` and `tools` are generated from `internal/scan`'s tables (§3.86),**
157	in `scan_fields.go`: a category or a tool added there appears here with no line
158	written for it.
159	
160	- **`scan`** is what a scan looks for: one checkbox per category, and under it
161	  one per tool when there is a choice (`Depth` 1, and 2 for a renderer under
162	  kubeconform). A category with one tool has no sub-row; its tool is its dimmed
163	  `Note`. A tool row is a `get`/`set` pair over the category's list rather
164	  than a pointer — the one exception to the pointer rule, since membership has
165	  no address. A tool's `Args` is the other: a text field backed by a list
166	  (`field.list`), edited as one line (`scan.SplitArgs`/`JoinArgs`, quotes keep
167	  a value with spaces together) and refused by name when it carries a flag
168	  DevDesk sets itself.
169	- **A checkbox can be `locked`**, with a reason the footer says in place of the
170	  hint: a part of Trivy a server cannot do, a category that is off, a renderer
171	  whose kubeconform is not ticked. A locked box keeps its tick
172	  (`theme.RenderCheckboxLocked`), and the cursor stops on it. **A server no
173	  longer unticks anything**: the scanner skips what it cannot do
174	  (`Scanner.wants`), so switching the server off gives back what was there.
175	- **A `guard` refuses a value**: unticking the last tool of a category that is
176	  on (`reasonLastTool`) — the category's own box is the switch for "none".
177	- **A checkbox explains both of its states** (`hintOn`/`hintOff`, read by
178	  `Model.hint`): the footer says what the box does as it is, and changes as
179	  `space` is pressed. `TestEveryCheckboxExplainsBothStates` covers both tabs.
180	- **`tools`** is one group per tool, plus the platform tools (engine, git) as
181	  read-only rows. Each heading carries the tool's state — required and there,
182	  required and missing, or `not used` — from the router's detection
183	  (`shared.ScanToolsMsg`) and `scan.Required` over the categories being edited,
184	  so a box ticked on `scan` changes a heading at once. `ctrl+r` there asks the
185	  router to detect again; greyed on the other tabs (Rule 130).
186	- **Two columns** when the tab declares them and the width allows
187	  (`columnMinWidth` each), the groups split in order where the heights come
188	  closest: `↓` reads down the left column and on to the right, since the focus
189	  order is still the flat list. Each row is built by hand and fitted to its
190	  column (Rule 115).
191	
192	**Every tab scrolls.** `View` lays the whole tab out (`layout`), and
193	`keepFocusVisible` moves `scroll` after each key and resize so the focused
194	field and its heading are on screen. The scan tab alone ran past seventy lines,
195	and its bottom was simply cut off.
196	
197	**The header names the context, and the title does not.** A configuration
198	belongs to one, and editing `workspaces_dir` in the wrong context is otherwise
199	silent because the fields look identical in all of them — but that is what
200	`GetHeaderInfo` says here as it does in every other view, so a title repeating
201	it was the same fact twice on one screen. `GetTitle()` is `󰙨 Configuration`.
202	
203	**The context's file path is a row in the form, not a header field.** It sits in
204	**Paths** under `workspaces_dir`, because that is what it belongs beside; the
205	header is for what changes as the user moves, and the file does not. It is the
206	one `kindStatic` field — shown, never written, and `Model.settleFocus` walks the
207	cursor past it in whichever direction it was already moving, since a focus
208	indicator on a row no key acts upon says the opposite of what is true. The
209	**Paths** group therefore reads three paths and then the checkbox that qualifies
210	them (`show_hidden_files`): a checkbox wedged between two value rows breaks the
211	column they share.
212	
213	Chevrons and values are aligned on one column per tab, padded on the **head**
214	(label plus a cycle field's select icon) rather than on the label — padding the
215	label leaves a cycle field's chevron two cells right of every other. Checkboxes
216	are excluded from the measurement: they have no value, so a long checkbox label
217	would push every value right for nothing. `theme.RenderCheckbox` already emits
218	the focus indicator, so the view must not add a second.
219	
220	| Kind | Control | Persists |
221	|---|---|---|
222	| closed set | cycle `←→` (Rule 132) | immediately |
223	| boolean | checkbox, `Space` only | immediately |
224	| text / integer | `textinput` | on blur, **after validation** |
225	
226	**A refused value keeps the cursor on its field.** An unparseable integer or a
227	malformed Trivy address is reported (Rule 128) and *not* written — coercing to
228	zero is how `trivy_server: ":"` reached a config file in the first place.
229	
230	**"On blur" includes leaving the view, and that is what D62 was.** `commitFocused`
231	was reached from `switchTab` and `moveField` only, so `↑↓` and `tab` wrote and
232	nothing else did: a path typed and then abandoned with `ctrl+p` was never
233	applied. The router caches this view and `Init()` does nothing, so coming back
234	to `:cfg` showed the typed value while the file held the old one — the screen
235	confirmed the setting on every visit, which is what sent the search for the
236	defect into the scanner instead.
237	
238	Two things close it:
239	
240	- **`Leave()`**, the view's half of `app.LeavingView`. The router calls it
241	  before `switchView` and before `switchContext`, and a refusal **cancels the
242	  switch**. That is not a preference between the two options the backlog left
243	  open: the footer belongs to the view, so letting the user go and reporting the
244	  abandoned value there would post the message onto the screen that is leaving.
245	  The other answer cannot be *said*, and an unsayable answer is the same silence
246	  one layer down.
247	- **`esc` commits without moving.** It used to fall through to the input, which
248	  ignores it — the one gesture a user tries to close a field was the one that
249	  settled nothing. It re-binds the input afterwards, so `007` in an integer
250	  field becomes the `7` that was actually stored: telling a written value from a
251	  merely typed one is the other half of what made the defect durable.
252	
253	`esc` is announced although Rule 138 calls the key obvious, because what it does
254	here is not, and it is greyed on the fields where it would do nothing —
255	`settlesOnBlur` is that question, and it is exactly the set `commitFocused` acts
256	on: text, integer, `Forge` and `Secret backend`. A checkbox and an ordinary
257	cycle field have already written by the time the cursor could leave.
258	
259	Two settings are special-cased, matched by label:
260	
261	- **Theme** applies as it is cycled, not on blur — otherwise the user chooses
262	  blind.
263	- **Secret backend** is confirmed when focus *leaves* the field, not on every
264	  `←→`, and **nothing is migrated between backends**. §3.9 removed the option
265	  that wrote a token to two stores at once; copying one here would rebuild it.
266	  Declining restores the previous value.
267	
268	**`forge.url` belongs to this view, not to the auth view.** Both used to write
269	it, so neither was authoritative and editing it in one left the other stale. The
270	auth view now shows it read-only, points at `:config`, and owns only the token
271	and the act of logging in — which is where the §3.9 line falls: this view's
272	contract is "everything here goes to `config.yaml`", and a token never does.
273	
274	**`Forge` is the first field of the Connection group, above the URL.**
275	Everything below it reconfigures from it — the URL example, the visibility set,
276	two labels, the tab's own title and icon — so it has to be above them for the
277	user to watch that happen.
278	
279	It is a cycle field (Rule 132) whose values are `config.ForgeTypes()`, and it is
280	**settled on blur**, not on every `←→`: the change closes the session, and
281	cycling through the list would close it once per keypress, including on the way
282	back to where it started. That is the secret backend's shape, minus the
283	question — changing the platform is neither forbidden nor confirmed, the user is
284	told what it did.
285	
286	**Changing the URL *or* the platform closes the client-side session**
287	(`ForgeChanged` on the message) and says so. One flag for two settings, because
288	the consequence is one: the session was opened against something the config no
289	longer describes. Nothing is revoked and no token is deleted — the user changed
290	an address or a platform, not their credentials.
291	
292	The URL field is recognised by **accessor identity**
293	(`f.str(cfg) == &cfg.Forge.URL`), not by label: two tabs could both hold a field
294	called "URL".
295	
296	**The host is detected, and an explicit choice is never overwritten.**
297	`forge.DetectType` recognises `gitlab.com` and `github.com` and **nothing else**
298	— self-hosted is the case that matters and `git.acme.com` could be either, so an
299	unrecognised host changes nothing rather than guessing confidently. Detection
300	re-runs when the URL is committed, but only while `forgeTouched` is false: once
301	the user has moved the Forge field, typing a URL must not contradict them. That
302	flag is the whole difference between helpful and possessive. Probing
303	(`/api/v4/version` against `/api/v3/`) was rejected — a round trip per commit,
304	and it fails on instances that authenticate those endpoints.
305	
306	**Two things follow a platform change, and both would be silent bugs without
307	it.** The field table is rebuilt, because it is computed once from the type and
308	the router *keeps* this view on a save — so nothing else would. And a
309	`default_visibility` the new platform does not have is coerced to its most
310	private: GitHub.com has no `internal`, and a context carrying it would hold a
311	value the server refuses while the cycle field opened on a value absent from its
312	own list.
313	
314	`ConfigSavedMsg` goes to the router, which drops every view *except this one* so
315	they rebuild against the saved config — keeping the configuration view is what
316	stops a save throwing away the cursor after every keystroke. `BackendChanged`
317	is separate because it is the one change no view can rebuild itself into: the
318	router has to resolve a fresh `credentials.Selection`.

1	package agentusage
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"strconv"
7		"time"
8	)
9	
10	// lineKind classifies one transcript line.
11	type lineKind int
12	
13	const (
14		kindUsage      lineKind = iota // message.usage present: counts
15		kindNoUsage                    // message with an id, but no usage object
16		kindIgnored                    // valid JSON without a message, or a message with neither id, model nor usage
17		kindUnreadable                 // not JSON, truncated, or bad counters
18		kindSynthetic                  // model "<synthetic>": never counts
19	)
20	
21	// record is what decodeLine extracts from a line; only these fields are read.
22	type record struct {
23		MessageID string
24		Model     string
25		Version   string
26		Usage     Tokens
27		StopNull  bool
28		At        time.Time // root timestamp in UTC; zero if absent or not a date
29		Tools     []toolRef // tool_use blocks of a non-synthetic assistant line
30	}
31	
32	// toolRef is one tool_use block of an assistant line.
33	type toolRef struct {
34		id  string // tool_use id; "" if absent or not a string
35		abi int    // the line's apiBlockIndex; -1 when absent
36		idx int    // position of the block in message.content
37	}
38	
39	// wireBlock keeps a content block's type and id only: nothing else of a block
40	// (text, tool input, tool output) is ever declared, so none is kept.
41	type wireBlock struct{ Type, ID string }
42	
43	// toolUseType is the content block type of a tool call.
44	const toolUseType = "tool_use"
45	
46	// blockAt is a tool_use block with its position in message.content.
47	type blockAt struct {
48		idx int
49		wireBlock
50	}
51	
52	// wireBlocks decodes message.content keeping the tool_use blocks only, as
53	// type and id: no text, tool input or tool output is retained. Content of
54	// another shape, and elements of another shape, yield no block and no error,
55	// so a malformed content costs the tool count of its line and nothing else.
56	type wireBlocks []blockAt
57	
58	// UnmarshalJSON implements json.Unmarshaler.
59	func (bs *wireBlocks) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
60		*bs = nil
61		// Unmarshal into a slice rather than streaming through a json.Decoder: the
62		// decoder copies every element, tool input included, which is several
63		// times slower and allocates a multiple of the line's size.
64		// encoding/json keeps an empty slot for an element of the wrong type and
65		// reports an UnmarshalTypeError at the end, so positions are preserved
66		// (a numeric id leaves Type set); any other error, a syntax error say,
67		// ends the scan without keeping a partial result.
68		var raw []wireBlock
69		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &raw); err != nil {
70			var te *json.UnmarshalTypeError
71			if !errors.As(err, &te) {
72				return nil
73			}
74		}
75		for i, b := range raw {
76			if b.Type == toolUseType {
77				*bs = append(*bs, blockAt{idx: i, wireBlock: b})
78			}
79		}
80		return nil
81	}
82	
83	// assistantType is the root type of the lines whose tool_use blocks count.
84	const assistantType = "assistant"
85	
86	// syntheticModel is the model name of locally generated, never-billed turns.
87	const syntheticModel = "<synthetic>"
88	
89	// wireLine mirrors the only keys read from a transcript line. Content,
90	// tools and descriptions are deliberately not declared, so encoding/json
91	// skips them without keeping them. Of the root, only the type, the timestamp,
92	// apiBlockIndex and the version are read, besides the message; of
93	// message.content, only the type and id of tool_use blocks (wireBlocks).
94	type wireLine struct {
95		Type          json.RawMessage `json:"type"`
96		Timestamp     json.RawMessage `json:"timestamp"`
97		APIBlockIndex json.RawMessage `json:"apiBlockIndex"`
98		Version       json.RawMessage `json:"version"`
99		Message       *wireMessage    `json:"message"`
100	}
101	
102	type wireMessage struct {
103		ID         string          `json:"id"`
104		Model      json.RawMessage `json:"model"`
105		StopReason json.RawMessage `json:"stop_reason"`
106		Content    wireBlocks      `json:"content"`
107		Usage      *wireUsage      `json:"usage"`
108	}
109	
110	// wireUsage keeps counters raw so a negative, fractional or non-numeric
111	// value can be told apart from an absent one.
112	type wireUsage struct {
113		Input      json.RawMessage `json:"input_tokens"`
114		Output     json.RawMessage `json:"output_tokens"`
115		CacheRead  json.RawMessage `json:"cache_read_input_tokens"`
116		CacheWrite json.RawMessage `json:"cache_creation_input_tokens"`
117	}
118	
119	// decodeLine extracts the usage fields of one transcript line. A message
120	// without usage counts as kindNoUsage only if it has an id or a model (an
121	// assistant turn whose usage went missing or was renamed). It never
122	// reports a decoder error: those can quote line content, so a bad line is
123	// just kindUnreadable.
124	func decodeLine(b []byte) (record, lineKind) {
125		var w wireLine
126		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &w); err != nil {
127			return record{}, kindUnreadable
128		}
129		m := w.Message
130		at := parseTimestamp(w.Timestamp)
131		if m == nil {
132			return record{Version: sanitizeLabel(optString(w.Version)), At: at}, kindIgnored
133		}
134		rec := record{
135			MessageID: m.ID,
136			Model:     sanitizeLabel(optString(m.Model)),
137			Version:   sanitizeLabel(optString(w.Version)),
138			StopNull:  isNullOrAbsent(m.StopReason),
139			At:        at,
140		}
141		if rec.Model != syntheticModel && optString(w.Type) == assistantType {
142			rec.Tools = toolRefs(m.Content, parseBlockIndex(w.APIBlockIndex))
143		}
144		switch {
145		case rec.Model == syntheticModel:
146			return rec, kindSynthetic
147		case m.Usage == nil && m.ID == "" && rec.Model == "":
148			// User and tool-result lines carry a message without id, usage or model.
149			return rec, kindIgnored
150		case m.Usage == nil:
151			return rec, kindNoUsage
152		}
153		tokens, ok := m.Usage.tokens()
154		if !ok {
155			return record{}, kindUnreadable
156		}
157		rec.Usage = tokens
158		return rec, kindUsage
159	}
160	
161	// tokens converts the raw counters; ok is false if any is not a
162	// non-negative integer.
163	func (u *wireUsage) tokens() (Tokens, bool) {
164		var t Tokens
165		for _, c := range []struct {
166			raw json.RawMessage
167			dst *int64
168		}{{u.Input, &t.Input}, {u.Output, &t.Output}, {u.CacheRead, &t.CacheRead}, {u.CacheWrite, &t.CacheWrite}} {
169			n, ok := parseCounter(c.raw)
170			if !ok {
171				return Tokens{}, false
172			}
173			*c.dst = n
174		}
175		return t, true
176	}
177	
178	// parseCounter reads one counter; absent or null is 0.
179	func parseCounter(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
180		if len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null" {
181			return 0, true
182		}
183		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(string(raw), 10, 64)
184		return n, err == nil && n >= 0
185	}
186	
187	// optString returns the JSON string held by raw, or "" if raw is absent or
188	// of another type: metadata of an unexpected type must not cost the line.
189	func optString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
190		var s string
191		if len(raw) == 0 || raw[0] != '"' || json.Unmarshal(raw, &s) != nil {
192			return ""
193		}
194		return s
195	}
196	
197	// isNullOrAbsent reports whether raw is a missing key or a JSON null. Any
198	// other value, whatever its type, counts as a stop reason being set.
199	func isNullOrAbsent(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
200		return len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null"
201	}
202	
203	// parseTimestamp reads a root timestamp as an instant in UTC; anything else
204	// (absent, null, not a string, not RFC 3339) is the zero time.
205	func parseTimestamp(raw json.RawMessage) time.Time {
206		s := optString(raw)
207		if s == "" {
208			return time.Time{}
209		}
210		t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, s)
211		if err != nil {
212			return time.Time{}
213		}
214		return t.UTC()
215	}
216	
217	// parseBlockIndex reads apiBlockIndex; -1 if absent or not a non-negative integer.
218	func parseBlockIndex(raw json.RawMessage) int {
219		n, err := strconv.Atoi(string(raw))
220		if err != nil || n < 0 {
221			return -1
222		}
223		return n
224	}
225	
226	// toolRefs lists the tool calls of a line from its decoded content blocks.
227	func toolRefs(blocks wireBlocks, abi int) []toolRef {
228		var refs []toolRef
229		for _, b := range blocks {
230			refs = append(refs, toolRef{id: b.ID, abi: abi, idx: b.idx})
231		}
232		return refs
233	}

1	package agentusage
2	
3	import "time"
4	
5	// Agent is the usage of one agent of a session: the orchestrator (Main) or a
6	// sub-agent.
7	type Agent struct {
8		ID              string
9		Main            bool
10		Type            string // sub-agent type from its meta file; "" if unknown
11		Models          []string
12		Tokens          Tokens
13		Messages        int // distinct message ids
14		PartialMessages int // messages whose last line has no stop reason
15		State           State
16		SpawnDepth      int
17		ToolCalls       int       // distinct tool_use blocks of the agent's assistant lines
18		FirstActivity   time.Time // earliest line timestamp (UTC); zero if none
19		LastActivity    time.Time // latest line timestamp (UTC); zero if none
20		// key is the table's identity for the agent's lines (the rank of its
21		// transcript); empty means ID. finish clears it from its output.
22		key string
23	}
24	
25	// Duration is LastActivity - FirstActivity, or 0 unless both are known.
26	func (a Agent) Duration() time.Duration {
27		if a.FirstActivity.IsZero() || a.LastActivity.IsZero() {
28			return 0
29		}
30		return a.LastActivity.Sub(a.FirstActivity)
31	}
32	
33	// PartialOutput reports whether some message of the agent was still being
34	// written (no stop reason on its last line), so its output count is a floor.
35	func (a Agent) PartialOutput() bool { return a.PartialMessages > 0 }
36	
37	// IssueKind classifies a line that could not be counted.
38	type IssueKind int
39	
40	const (
41		IssueUnreadable IssueKind = iota // not JSON, truncated, or bad counters
42		IssueOversized                   // longer than MaxLineBytes
43		IssueOpenFailed                  // a sub-agent transcript could not be opened

24		// GitLab is what `forge:` replaced. Same treatment as Docker above, and for
25		// the same reason: a context targets one forge, so the section is named
26		// after the role rather than after the one implementation there was.
27		//
28		// Deprecated: use Forge.

30	}
31	
32	// MCPConfig governs the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP (§3.61).
33	//
34	// It was a read-only stdio subcommand, `dk mcp` (§3.38). Three of that entry's
35	// decisions were reversed together: an agent running in a container cannot
36	// execute the host binary, which was §3.38's own open question 1 and became the
37	// only case anyone had.
38	//
39	// Enabled is false by default and that is the whole safety story: turning it on
40	// is the moment the user decides an agent may reach this context. Nothing
41	// migrates it, and nothing turns it on as a side effect.
42	//
43	// **What it means widened with §3.61, and nothing re-asks.** Under §3.38 it
44	// meant a read-only server on stdio, started by the client, with no listener at
45	// all; it now opens a loopback port and — `expose` being empty by default —
46	// serves the action tier as well. A context that said yes to the first is not
47	// asked again about the second, and a file written before §3.61 is recognisable
48	// (it carries no `listen`), so a narrower default was available and was
49	// deliberately not taken: the setting has always meant "an agent may reach this
50	// context", the widening is the entry's whole subject, and a migration would be
51	// ceremony around a decision its only user had just made. It is written here
52	// rather than left for someone to discover.
53	//
54	// There is no setting for the `Match` of a secret finding, and its absence is
55	// the guarantee. The entry proposed `redact_secret_matches: true` while also
56	// classing the string itself as never exposed — a setting whose other value is
57	// refused is a parameter that has to be ignored (§3.39). Worse, `false` is a
58	// bool's zero value, so every file written before the key existed would decode
59	// to "do not redact": the exact shape of D12. The tool schemas simply have
60	// nowhere to carry the string, which is the guarantee `context_get` already
61	// gets by construction (§3.9).
62	type MCPConfig struct {
63		// Enabled decides whether the TUI serves at all. The refusal names this
64		// setting and the context, because activating it in the wrong one is
65		// otherwise an hour spent looking at a server that will not start.
66		Enabled bool `yaml:"enabled"`
67	
68		// Expose is an **allow-list** of tool names; empty means every declared
69		// tool. It is not a deny-list, for the reason §3.38 gives in the other
70		// direction: a tool never registered cannot fail to be excluded, whereas a
71		// deny-list is one forgotten line away from exposing what arrives next.
72		Expose []string `yaml:"expose,omitempty"`
73	
74		// Listen is the address the server binds, and it is a loopback address
75		// because that is both the most closed bind available and the one that
76		// works: on Docker Desktop a container reaching `host.docker.internal`
77		// arrives at the host's loopback, so a sandboxed agent is served without
78		// the LAN ever being offered the port. The sandbox's own network policy is
79		// a second lock — the port has to be allowed there by name.
80		//
81		// It is a setting rather than a literal for one reason, and it is not
82		// configurability: on native Linux Docker `host.docker.internal` does not
83		// reach the host's loopback, and the bridge gateway would have to be bound
84		// instead. That case does not exist here and is not handled — but a literal
85		// would have to be rewritten, where a setting has to be documented.
86		//
87		// An empty value means the default, never "listen nowhere": the zero value
88		// of a string cannot be allowed to read as a choice, which is the shape of
89		// D12. applyDefaults fills it.
90		Listen string `yaml:"listen,omitempty"`
91	}
92	
93	// DefaultMCPListen is where the server binds when the context does not say.
94	//
95	// Loopback, and a port high enough to be out of the way. It is named rather
96	// than inlined because applyDefaults and Default both need it, and a second
97	// literal is how the two drift.
98	const DefaultMCPListen = "127.0.0.1:7777"

61	// gets by construction (§3.9).
62	type MCPConfig struct {
63		// Enabled decides whether the TUI serves at all. The refusal names this
64		// setting and the context, because activating it in the wrong one is
65		// otherwise an hour spent looking at a server that will not start.
66		Enabled bool `yaml:"enabled"`
